title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recorder: Fireflies.ai

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review the latest quality evals from the prompt set we ran, look at regressions in the new quantized variant, confirm guardrails behavior on PII, and agree next steps for the 2k sample benchmark. AE/SE present from Redwood, AtlasPay trial team on call.

Topics:
- Results review: scoring rubric and aggregated metrics
- Regression identified in 'billing' intent prompts after quantize-ggml change
- Guardrails: PII redaction and false positives
- Tuning: prompt engineering and temperature/best-of settings, partial rollouts
- Ops ask: run 2k full run on dedicated pool and share raw outputs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, um let's do a quick roll call. maya here on AE side, jared is on for SE and lina from csm.
[00:07] Sofia (AtlasPay): hey hi, sofia here, dan, priya and oliver are with me.
[00:10] Jared (Redwood SE): great, quick agenda, we'll run through the evaluation spreadsheet you shared, go over two regression cases you flagged and then action items. feel free to jump in.
[00:20] Dan: yes, thanks. we pushed last week's prompt set through the runner this morning, and the summary sheet shows a drop in exact-match for billing intents from 92% to 78% after the new quantized variant. not sure why.
[00:34] Jared: okay that aligns with what we saw — likely the quantize-ggml profile changed tokenization at the margins, and there was also a model variant swap — can you confirm which model label you used?
[00:45] Priya: we used redwood-v2-small-quant (the one from the drop-in). the pipeline defaulted to that after we applied the recommended config.
[00:55] Jared: got it. so two possible vectors: model variant semantic shift, or prompt sensitivity introduced by different temperature defaults during the conversion. can you show the example diffs?
[01:05] Dan: sure sending screen, here are two examples 1) user asks "why was i charged twice" and model responded with generic billing policy instead of account-specific last-payment info, so it masked the account lookup step.
[01:20] Sofia: and in second case it hallucinated an invoice number.
[01:25] Maya: hallucination plus redaction mismatch, yeah. okay. jared, can we reproduce this on hosted before we spin up dedicated? we want to know if it's model-only or infra/quantization.
[01:35] Jared: yes, we ran a quick reproducer — on hosted with the same model label we saw similar drop, so it's likely model/quant tie. but there are also slight differences when you run on dedicated with continuous batching; kv cache handling can change token alignment but usually not that magnitude.
[01:50] Oliver (Security): quick Q on guardrails — our requirement is that PII (SSNs, bank acct) should never be returned verbatim. we saw one false positive where the model redacted something that wasn't PII and another where it returned a partial masked SSN. what are the guardrail options?
[02:05] Lina (CSM): we have a couple: 1) Redwood Optimize rule-based post-filtering that removes or masks patterns, 2) prompt-level guardrails to instruct model to refuse with a template, 3) privacy plugin that adds deterministic redaction pre-send.
[02:18] Jared: recommend layered approach: pre-send regex + model refusal + post-filter. regex eliminates most straightforward cases, refusal covers ambiguous, and post-filter is a safety net for model slip-through. we'll share the rulebook.
[02:30] Sofia: sounds good. for scoring, we use exact-match + semantic similarity (embedding cosine) + a custom severity weight for hallucinations. current rubric: exact 0.6, semantic 0.3, hallucination penalty 0.1. does that align with your suggestions?
[02:45] Maya: that's reasonable but I'd bump hallucination penalty to 0.15 for customer-facing flows like billing, because cost of wrong info is high. also tie a threshold for auto-pass vs manual review.
[02:58] Priya: question on tooling: can we attach the raw model logits or top-k candidates to flagged cases for debugging?
[03:06] Jared: hosted doesn't expose raw logits by default, but for Dedicated or Private you can enable debug dumps. alternative is we can return top-5 completions in the runner for a controlled set.
[03:18] Dan: for the 2k run we want top-5 and token-level alignments where possible.
[03:23] Jared: noted. we'll provision a dedicated small pool for the 2k run — it'll let us toggle quant profiles consistently.
[03:30] Sofia: another regression detail — the scoring sheet shows a spike in false positives for PII masking after canonicalization step; looks like normalization changed punctuation handling.
[03:40] Maya: normalization differences are a classic migration smell. jared, is there a canonical tokenizer diff tool?
[03:46] Jared: yes, we have a token-diff utility in the onboarding repo that highlights tokenization changes between model builds; i'll share link. it helped us root cause a similar billing regression last quarter.
[03:55] Oliver: on compliance, we also need to log every decision where the model refuses or redacts — a tamper-evident audit log. can Redwood provide that?
[04:05] Lina: yes, Private and Dedicated can surface audit logs with event types; hosted has a long-form trace but for SOC2 you'd want dedicated with KMS and audit retention.
[04:15] Priya: timeline question — if we run the 2k benchmark and see the regression persist, what's patch path? revert to previous model variant or prompt hack?
[04:24] Jared: short term revert to last-good model label is simplest; medium term we can tune prompts and guardrails; long term we work with model team/quant profile to retrain conversion. we'll help with canary rollout so only a portion of traffic sees the new variant.
[04:36] Maya: ok let's capture action items. also, sofia asked for a short write-up on recommended scoring threshold adjustments.
[04:45] Sofia: yep and please include examples for manual review criteria.
[04:50] Maya: perfect. any final Qs?
[04:55] Dan: none from me.
[04:57] Priya: no.
[04:58] Oliver: nope.
[04:59] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the runner link and schedule a deep dive on quantization if needed.

End of transcript.
summary: Weekly POC sync covering quality regressions observed after applying a quantized model variant. Team agreed regression likely model/quantization related; plan to run 2k benchmark on dedicated pool with top-5 outputs and token alignments. Guardrails strategy is layered (pre-send regex, refusal prompt, post-filter). Action items assigned for reproducer, token-diff, and scoring thresholds.
action_items: Jared Kim (SE): share token-diff utility link and quick repro steps (due: 2025-06-12)
Maya Patel (AE): send updated scoring recommendation doc with higher hallucination weight (due: 2025-06-11)
AtlasPay - Dan Li: provide sample 120 failure cases and raw outputs from your runner (due: 2025-06-12)
Lina Torres (CSM): provision small dedicated pool for 2k run and share access (due: 2025-06-13)
Redwood: enable top-5 runner output for flagged cases and include token alignments where possible (due: 2025-06-13)
next_steps: Run 2k benchmark on dedicated pool with top-5 outputs and token alignments
If regression persists, revert to last-good model variant and do canary rollout
Share guardrail rulebook and regex patterns for PII masking
Schedule deep dive on quantization with Redwood infra team (propose times in next email)
